fasteners.captive_nut_slot.summary: Negative (subtract me) side-entry slot for a captive hex nut plus the screw clearance hole.

params.name: size
params.description: nut size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: slot_length
params.description: how far the entry slot runs from the nut centre in +X (reach the part's edge)

params.name: nut_clearance
params.description: added across flats so the nut slides in

params.name: thickness_clearance
params.description: added to nut thickness

params.name: screw_depth_above
params.description: screw clearance hole length in +Z above the nut

params.name: screw_depth_below
params.description: screw clearance hole length in -Z below the nut

params.name: screw_oversize
params.description: FDM oversize on the screw hole

material_notes.orientation: nut axis vertical; if the slot roof is a horizontal bridge keep slot_length short or add a sacrificial layer

fasteners.captive_nut_slot.docstring:
Cutter centred on the nut, nut mid-plane at z=0, slot running in +X.

Example:
    body = body - Pos(x, y, z_nut) * captive_nut_slot("M3", slot_length=wall_to_edge)
fasteners.captive_nut_slot.example: body = body - Pos(x, y, z_nut) * captive_nut_slot("M3", slot_length=wall_to_edge)

fasteners.clearance_hole.summary: Negative (subtract me) clearance hole for a metric screw, with print oversize and optional counterbore or countersink.

params.name: size
params.description: screw size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: depth
params.description: hole length along -Z from the surface at z=0 (make it through the whole part)

params.name: fit
params.description: ISO 273 series: fine, medium, coarse

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: added to diameter because FDM holes print small (0.2-0.4 typical)

params.name: head
params.description: none, counterbore (socket head) or countersink (90 deg)

params.name: head_clearance
params.description: added to head diameter for counterbore/countersink

params.name: head_depth
params.description: counterbore depth; default = head height

material_notes.orientation: any; for horizontal holes use primitives.teardrop instead

fasteners.clearance_hole.docstring:
Cutter whose top face sits at z=0 and extends downward ``depth``.

Example:
    plate = plate - [Pos(x, y, plate_t) * clearance_hole("M3", depth=plate_t) for x, y in pts]
fasteners.clearance_hole.example: plate = plate - [Pos(x, y, plate_t) * clearance_hole("M3", depth=plate_t) for x, y in pts]

fasteners.heat_set_boss.summary: Cylindrical boss with a correctly sized pocket for a brass heat-set insert.

params.name: size
params.description: insert size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: height
params.description: total boss height from its base (z=0) to the insert face

params.name: wall
params.description: plastic wall around the insert hole; defaults to the insert's minimum

params.name: pocket_depth
params.description: insert pocket depth; default = insert length + 1 mm for melt relief

params.name: top_chamfer
params.description: lead-in chamfer at the mouth of the pocket (helps the insert seat square)

params.name: base_fillet
params.description: fillet where the boss meets its parent surface (0 = none)

params.name: through
params.description: make the pocket a through hole (for bosses on thin floors)

material_notes.orientation: boss axis vertical (insert pressed in along Z); pocket walls are then continuous perimeters
material_notes.notes: Insert pocket is sized per the insert spec, never per the screw. In PLA keep iron at ~200 C.

fasteners.heat_set_boss.docstring:
Boss standing on z=0 with an insert pocket opening at the top.

The boss is centred on the origin so it can be placed with a Location::

Example:
    from lib.component import locations_of
    from lib.patterns.pi import pi5_mount
    bosses = Part() + [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5", height=6) for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]
    floor = floor + bosses
fasteners.heat_set_boss.example:
from lib.component import locations_of
from lib.patterns.pi import pi5_mount
bosses = Part() + [loc * heat_set_boss("M2.5", height=6) for loc in locations_of(pi5_mount())]
floor = floor + bosses

fasteners.heat_set_pocket.summary: Negative (subtract me) pocket for a heat-set insert in a solid wall or floor.

params.name: size
params.description: insert size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: depth
params.description: pocket depth; default = insert length + 1 mm

params.name: extra
params.description: extra height above z=0 so the cutter clears the surface cleanly

material_notes.orientation: pocket axis vertical preferred

fasteners.heat_set_pocket.docstring:
Cylinder to subtract; its top face sits at z=0 (the wall surface) and it
extends downward by ``depth``.

Example:
    lid = lid - [loc * heat_set_pocket("M3") for loc in locations_of(holes)]
fasteners.heat_set_pocket.example: lid = lid - [loc * heat_set_pocket("M3") for loc in locations_of(holes)]

fasteners.screw_boss.summary: Boss with a pilot hole for a machine screw to self-thread into printed plastic.

params.name: size
params.description: screw size: M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5

params.name: height
params.description: boss height from z=0

params.name: wall
params.description: wall around the pilot (>= 2 perimeters, 1.6 mm recommended for M3)

params.name: pilot_d
params.description: pilot hole diameter; default from hardware table (thread-forming size)

params.name: pilot_depth
params.description: pilot depth; default = full height minus one wall thickness of floor

params.name: top_chamfer
params.description: entry chamfer

params.name: base_fillet
params.description: fillet at the base (0 = none)

material_notes.orientation: boss axis vertical so the screw threads cut across layers, not between them
material_notes.notes: Good for ~5 insert/remove cycles. Use heat_set_boss for anything serviced often. PLA cracks under over-torque.

fasteners.screw_boss.docstring:
Boss standing on z=0, pilot hole opening at the top.

Example:
    boss = screw_boss("M3", height=10)
    body = body + Pos(20, 10, floor_t) * boss
fasteners.screw_boss.example:
boss = screw_boss("M3", height=10)
body = body + Pos(20, 10, floor_t) * boss

form.ball_chain.summary: Chain of overlapping ellipsoids at given (x, y, z, r): the part of a creature that leaves the ground — a reared neck, a tentacle, a raised tail — which a dome_chain cannot do.

params.name: balls
params.description: sequence of (x, y, z, r); neighbours must overlap to make one solid

params.name: squash
params.description: Z scale per ball: 1.0 = a sphere, >1 = a taller egg

material_notes.orientation: a ball floating free is a 90 deg overhang all round its underside: every ball must sit ON something — the one below it, or a body it is half sunk into — and a rearing chain must lean IN as it rises, never out
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. This is the one blob primitive that can print unsupported nonsense, so check the overhang number after using it, not just the fit.

form.ball_chain.docstring:
Overlapping ellipsoids in 3D, the way ``dome_cluster`` overlaps half-ellipsoids in a plane.

Example:
    neck = ball_chain(((0, 0, 10, 10), (0, -6, 20, 8.5), (0, -10, 29, 7)), squash=1.1)

form.blob_outline.summary: Smoothed union of circles as a sketch (blob / pebble / organic plate outline).

params.name: circles
params.description: sequence of (x, y, r); neighbours must overlap

params.name: smooth_r
params.description: fillet radius at every junction (0 = none)

material_notes.orientation: any (2D outline)
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED

form.cloud_outline.summary: Cloud silhouette sketch: flat edge at -Y, round lobes bulging toward +Y; centred on the origin.

params.name: length
params.description: X extent

params.name: width
params.description: Y extent, flat edge (y = -width/2) to the tallest lobe (y = +width/2)

params.name: lobes
params.description: relative lobe radii left to right, e.g. (0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 0.85, 0.7); 1.0 = lobe_r

params.name: lobe_r
params.description: largest lobe radius; None = 0.22 * length

params.name: overlap
params.description: how far lobe centres sink below the base top, as a fraction of their radius

params.name: smooth_r
params.description: fillet radius where lobes meet each other and the base

material_notes.orientation: any (2D outline)
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED

form.cloud_outline.docstring:
Base = rounded rectangle from the flat edge up; lobes = circles along the base top, spread so the
outer lobes are flush with the base sides.  Rotate the sketch to put the flat edge where you need it.

Example:
    tray = extrude(cloud_outline(130, 95), amount=2) + extrude(cloud_outline(130, 95) - offset(cloud_outline(130, 95), -1.6), amount=8)
form.cloud_outline.example: tray = extrude(cloud_outline(130, 95), amount=2) + extrude(cloud_outline(130, 95) - offset(cloud_outline(130, 95), -1.6), amount=8)

form.dome_chain.summary: Chain of overlapping domes stepped along a spline path at equal spacing, tapering head to tail: caterpillars, snakes, larvae, vines, bunting.

params.name: path
params.description: sequence of (x, y) control points the body follows, head first; the chain starts on the first and ends on the last

params.name: count
params.description: number of segments

params.name: r_head
params.description: radius of the first segment

params.name: r_tail
params.description: radius of the last segment

params.name: squash
params.description: Z scale per dome: 1.0 = hemisphere, >1 = a taller, rounder body

params.name: base_z
params.description: plane the flat faces sit on

params.name: smooth
params.description: True: a spline through the control points; False: straight runs between them

material_notes.orientation: flat faces down: an upper half-ellipsoid has no down-facing surface, so any squash >= 1 needs no support
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. Neighbours only fuse where they OVERLAP, and the spacing is the path length over count-1: a long path with few segments gives a row of separate beads. Rule of thumb, keep count above path_length / r_tail.

form.dome_chain.docstring:
A body that follows a line instead of a list of coordinates.

Stepping at equal ARC length is the point: sampling a spline by its own parameter bunches the
segments up on the straight runs and stretches them thin round the corners, which on a creature
reads immediately as a mistake.  Radii interpolate head to tail over the same steps.

Example:
    body = dome_chain(((0, 0), (20, -12), (44, -6)), count=9, r_head=11, r_tail=4, squash=1.5)
form.dome_chain.example: body = dome_chain(((0, 0), (20, -12), (44, -6)), count=9, r_head=11, r_tail=4, squash=1.5)

form.dome_cluster.summary: Union of dome blobs (upper half-ellipsoids) at given (x, y, r), flat faces on a common plane: caterpillar and creature bodies, pebbles, cloud lobes, bumpy grips.

params.name: domes
params.description: sequence of (x, y, r); neighbours must overlap to make one solid

params.name: squash
params.description: Z scale per dome: 1.0 = hemisphere, >1 = taller egg, <1 = flat pebble

params.name: base_z
params.description: plane the flat faces sit on; pass a value below a ground surface to half-bury them

material_notes.orientation: flat faces down on the bed (or on the body that carries them): an upper half-ellipsoid has no down-facing surface at all, so any squash >= 1 needs no support
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. squash < 1 flattens the dome and starts to add a shallow overhang near the rim; keep it above ~0.7 unless the cluster is supported. Domes that only touch become separate solids — overlap them.

form.dome_cluster.docstring:
Overlapping domes as one solid, the way ``blob_outline`` overlaps circles in 2D.

A dome of radius ``r`` rises ``r * squash`` above ``base_z``.  Sink the cluster into whatever
carries it (``base_z`` a few mm below the ground surface) rather than resting it on top: a blob
that merely shares a face with the plate under it fuses into a separate loose solid.

Example:
    body = ground + dome_cluster(((0, 0, 12), (13, 1, 10), (23, -4, 8)), squash=1.4, base_z=-3)

form.drain_holes.summary: Planter drainage: one centre hole plus a ring of holes, as a sketch to subtract from a floor.

params.name: ring_r
params.description: radius of the hole ring

params.name: hole_d
params.description: hole diameter

params.name: count
params.description: holes on the ring

params.name: centre
params.description: also cut a centre hole

material_notes.orientation: any (2D pattern)
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED

form.flutes.summary: Cut vertical flutes into (or raise ribs on) the outer surface of any body, following its profile; polar array about Z.

params.name: shape
params.description: body to flute (Part); None = revolved_body() default

params.name: count
params.description: number of flutes around Z

params.name: width
params.description: flute width (tangential)

params.name: depth
params.description: cut depth into the surface (or rib height when raised)

params.name: z_from
params.description: flutes start height

params.name: z_to
params.description: flutes end height; None = full height

params.name: twist_angle
params.description: rotation of the flutes over their height (0 = straight)

params.name: raised
params.description: True: add ribs standing proud of the surface instead of cutting grooves

params.name: reference
params.description: optional solid used to derive the surface band (pass the un-shelled solid when fluting a shell)

material_notes.orientation: axis vertical, base on the bed
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: no test print yet; keep flute depth <= wall - 0.8 unless shelled afterwards

form.flutes.docstring:
``count`` radial bars, trimmed to the outer ``depth`` of ``reference`` (or ``shape``), are cut
from the shape, so the flute floor follows the body profile at constant depth.  Sharp-edged: no fillets.  Shell FIRST, then flute the shell with the solid as
``reference`` (offsetting a fluted solid is slow and often invalid); the wall under a flute is
then ``wall - depth``, so keep that >= 0.8 unless the part prints in spiral (vase) mode.

Example:
    solid = revolved_body(profile)
    vase = flutes(shell_open_top(solid, wall=2.0), count=20, width=3, depth=1.2, z_from=5, reference=solid)
form.flutes.example:
solid = revolved_body(profile)
vase = flutes(shell_open_top(solid, wall=2.0), count=20, width=3, depth=1.2, z_from=5, reference=solid)

form.revolved_body.summary: Solid of revolution about Z from an (r, z) profile, spline-smoothed by default, base on z=0 (vases, planters, lamps, knobs).

params.name: profile
params.description: sequence of (radius, z) points from the base rim (z=0) to the top rim; closed along the axis

params.name: smooth
params.description: True: one spline through the points; False: straight segments (facetted / stepped profiles)

params.name: tangents
params.description: optional start and end tangent directions for the spline, e.g. ((0, 1), (-1, 1)); None = natural

material_notes.orientation: axis vertical, base on the bed
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: no test print yet; designed for spiral (vase) mode or 2-4 perimeters

form.revolved_body.docstring:
The profile's last point is the top rim radius; the top is closed flat.  ``shell_open_top``
hollows it; ``flutes`` (with this solid as ``reference``) ribs the shell.

Example:
    solid = revolved_body(((30, 0), (34, 30), (26, 80), (30, 100)))
    vase = flutes(shell_open_top(solid, wall=2.0), count=20, reference=solid)
form.revolved_body.example:
solid = revolved_body(((30, 0), (34, 30), (26, 80), (30, 100)))
vase = flutes(shell_open_top(solid, wall=2.0), count=20, reference=solid)

form.sdf_solid.summary: Mesh a signed-distance function (positive inside) over a box with manifold3d level_set; default is a gyroid block.

params.name: sdf
params.description: callable f(x, y, z) -> float, positive inside; None = gyroid_sdf()

params.name: bounds
params.type: tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]
params.description: (xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax) of the evaluation box; the solid is clipped to it

params.name: edge_length
params.description: target triangle edge (resolution); 0.5-1.0 mm is plenty for FDM

material_notes.orientation: any; check overhangs, gyroids self-support up to ~cell 15 mm
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED

form.sdf_solid.docstring:
Example:
block = sdf_solid(gyroid_sdf(cell=12, thickness=1.2), bounds=(-20, -20, 0, 20, 20, 40))
lamp = mesh_boolean(block, cylinder_shape, "intersection")
form.sdf_solid.example:
block = sdf_solid(gyroid_sdf(cell=12, thickness=1.2), bounds=(-20, -20, 0, 20, 20, 40))
lamp = mesh_boolean(block, cylinder_shape, "intersection")

form.shell_open_top.summary: Hollow a solid into an open-top shell of uniform wall (floor included); default hollows the default revolved_body.

params.name: shape
params.description: solid to hollow (Part); None = revolved_body() default

params.name: wall
params.description: wall and floor thickness (multiple of 0.4)

material_notes.orientation: axis vertical, base on the bed
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: no test print yet; designed for spiral (vase) mode or 2-4 perimeters

form.shell_open_top.docstring:
The highest planar face becomes the opening; uniform inward offset (wall = floor).  Shell the
smooth solid, then add flutes / textures: offsetting an already-fluted body is slow and fragile.

Example:
    vase = shell_open_top(revolved_body(profile), wall=1.2)

form.surface_studs.summary: Domes seated where each ray first meets a body's surface, aligned with the local normal: toadstool spots, caterpillar tubercles, eyes, rivets, grip bumps.

params.name: shape
params.description: body to seat the studs on (Part); None = dome_cluster() default

params.name: rays
params.type: Sequence[tuple[tuple[float, float, float], tuple[float, float, float]]]
params.description: sequence of (origin, direction); the origin must be OUTSIDE the body and the stud lands on the first surface the ray meets

params.name: radius
params.description: stud radius (or a sequence, one per ray)

params.name: height
params.description: stud height above the surface; None = radius, i.e. a hemisphere

params.name: embed
params.description: how far the stud's flat base is sunk below the surface; it must exceed the surface's sag across the stud (about radius^2 / 2 / local_radius) or the stud only touches at a point and fuses into a loose solid

material_notes.orientation: a stud on a down-facing surface is an unsupported overhang; keep them on upward and sideways faces
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. A ray that misses the body is skipped silently, so check the stud count against the ray count when a spot goes missing.

form.surface_studs.docstring:
Studs on any surface, found by ray casting rather than by solving the surface analytically.

The point of casting instead of computing is that the same call decorates a body of revolution,
a dome cluster or a boxy part: aim a ray at the feature and the stud lands flat on whatever is
there, tilted with the surface.  Sink each one (``embed``) — a flat-based dome resting on a
convex surface touches it at exactly one point, and one point is not a union.

Example:
    cap = revolved_body(profile)
    spots = surface_studs(cap, [((x, y, 60), (0, 0, -1)) for x, y in dots], radius=2.4)
form.surface_studs.example:
cap = revolved_body(profile)
spots = surface_studs(cap, [((x, y, 60), (0, 0, -1)) for x, y in dots], radius=2.4)

form.textured.summary: Displace a shape's outer surface with Perlin noise or horizontal ripples and return a mesh (organic skin, hammered / wavy look).

params.name: shape
params.description: Part or mesh to texture; None = default hollow revolved_body

params.name: amplitude
params.description: peak displacement along the normal

params.name: scale
params.description: feature size (noise wavelength / ripple pitch)

params.name: kind
params.description: noise | ripple

params.name: mask
params.description: exterior (outer skin only, cavities and bosses untouched) | sides (|normal z| < 0.5) | all

params.name: seed
params.description: noise seed

params.name: edge_length
params.description: mesh refinement before displacing (smaller = finer texture, more triangles)

params.name: bed_margin
params.description: height above the bed left undisplaced (elephant-foot chamfer zone)

params.name: octaves
params.description: noise detail levels

material_notes.orientation: as the source shape; bed face is never displaced
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: texture amplitude <= 0.4 mm prints cleanly with 0.4 mm nozzle; larger needs slower outer walls

form.textured.docstring:
Refines the mesh to ``edge_length`` with manifold3d, then warps vertices along their normals
(horizontally only, unless ``mask="all"``, so no height changes).  The bed face and everything
below ``bed_margin`` stay put; ``exterior`` mask also keeps inner walls, bosses and holes exact so
fits are unchanged.  Returns a ``trimesh.Trimesh``; put it last in build().

Example:
    tray = textured(tray_part, amplitude=0.35, scale=6, mask="exterior")

form.twist.summary: Extrude a section along Z while rotating it (spiral / twisted vase body), base on z=0.

params.name: section
params.description: sketch to extrude (one or more faces); None = wavy_circle()

params.name: height
params.description: extrusion height

params.name: angle
params.description: total rotation over the height (sign = handedness)

params.name: taper
params.description: top scale relative to the base (1.0 = straight; 0.8 = narrows to 80 %)

material_notes.orientation: axis vertical, base on the bed
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED; keep the surface slope (angle * radius / height) under ~50 deg from vertical

form.twist.docstring:
Twist about the Z axis through the sketch origin.  ``taper`` != 1 is done by lofting rotated,
scaled copies of the section (slower, still exact enough at 2 deg per step).

Example:
    body = twist(wavy_circle(30, 3, 8), height=120, angle=90)
    vase = shell_open_top(body, wall=1.2)
form.twist.example:
body = twist(wavy_circle(30, 3, 8), height=120, angle=90)
vase = shell_open_top(body, wall=1.2)

form.voronoi_cells.summary: Voronoi cell openings as a sketch on a width x height panel, webbed, corner-rounded and roofed so each cell prints without support; periodic in X so it wraps seamlessly.

params.name: width
params.description: panel X extent, centred on the origin; wrap this around a cylinder of width/tau radius for a seamless join

params.name: height
params.description: panel Y extent, centred on the origin

params.name: count
params.description: number of cells

params.name: seed
params.description: random seed; change it for a different arrangement at the same statistics

params.name: web
params.description: material left between neighbouring cells (each cell is inset by half of it)

params.name: corner_r
params.description: fillet radius on every cell corner

params.name: roof_angle
params.description: slope of the two roof edges clipped off the top of each cell, from horizontal; 0 = leave cells unroofed (flat ceilings)

params.name: relax
params.description: Lloyd relaxation rounds; 0 = raw random cells (slivers and caverns), 2-3 = even cells

material_notes.orientation: panel Y is the print Z direction — the roof clip only self-supports if the cells are used that way up
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. Keep web >= 4 nozzle widths (1.6 mm at 0.4) or the webs print as single unbonded strands. roof_angle must stay at or above the slicer's overhang limit (45 deg is the usual limit; 50-55 leaves margin).

form.voronoi_cells.docstring:
The cell openings (the holes, not the webs) as one sketch of disjoint faces.

Subtract it from a flat panel, or hand it to ``voronoi_shell`` to wrap it around a body.

Example:
    vents = voronoi_cells(80, 30, count=18, web=2.0)
    panel = extrude(Rectangle(80, 30) - vents, amount=2)
form.voronoi_cells.example:
vents = voronoi_cells(80, 30, count=18, web=2.0)
panel = extrude(Rectangle(80, 30) - vents, amount=2)

form.voronoi_shell.summary: NEGATIVE component: Voronoi cells wrapped around a cylinder as radial prisms, to pierce the wall of a body of revolution (or dimple it) with self-supporting cells.

params.name: radius
params.description: radius the pattern is laid out on; use the body's mean radius over the band so the cells come out the size you asked for

params.name: height
params.description: Z extent of the band, centred on z=0 (translate the cutter to place it)

params.name: count
params.description: number of cells around the whole body

params.name: seed
params.description: random seed

params.name: web
params.description: material left between neighbouring cells

params.name: corner_r
params.description: fillet radius on every cell corner

params.name: roof_angle
params.description: slope of each cell's roof from horizontal; the ceiling of every hole, so keep it at or above the overhang limit

params.name: relax
params.description: Lloyd relaxation rounds

params.name: inner
params.description: radius the cutters stop at; put it inside the bore (or inside the far wall) so every cell breaks clean through, and remember the web there is only web * inner / radius

params.name: over
params.description: how far the cutters start outside the layout radius; must exceed how far the body bulges past it

material_notes.orientation: body axis vertical, base on the bed
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED. Each cell sits on the tangent plane at its own centre and fans in tangentially toward the axis, so the wrap is faceted: keep cells under about a third of the radius or the cut edges visibly skew. Check the web at the INNER radius, not at the layout radius — that is where it is narrowest and where a lattice fails.

form.voronoi_shell.docstring:
The lattice as a solid to subtract, band centred on z=0 and the body's axis on Z.

Each cell is lofted between a copy of itself at ``radius + over`` and a tangentially narrowed
copy at ``inner``, both at the same heights: the cell fans in like a wedge of an orange, which
keeps the webs, and only the height stays true so the roof keeps the angle it was cut at.

Example:
    stalk = revolved_body(profile) - Cylinder(5.8, 40)
    stalk -= Pos(0, 0, 16) * voronoi_shell(radius=9.4, height=14, count=18, web=2.2, inner=3.5)
form.voronoi_shell.example:
stalk = revolved_body(profile) - Cylinder(5.8, 40)
stalk -= Pos(0, 0, 16) * voronoi_shell(radius=9.4, height=14, count=18, web=2.2, inner=3.5)

form.wavy_circle.summary: Circle with a sinusoidal radius (lobed / scalloped section) as a sketch, for twisted vases and lamp shades.

params.name: radius
params.description: mean radius

params.name: amplitude
params.description: radial wave amplitude (peak = radius + amplitude)

params.name: lobes
params.description: number of waves around the circumference

params.name: phase
params.description: rotates the pattern

params.name: samples_per_lobe

mechanisms.cantilever_latch.summary: Cantilever snap-fit hook: flexing beam along +Z from z=0 with a ramped hook on the +X face at the tip.

params.name: length
params.description: beam length from root (z=0) to the underside of the hook

params.name: width
params.description: beam width (Y)

params.name: thickness
params.description: beam thickness (X) — the flexing dimension

params.name: hook_depth
params.description: how far the hook protrudes in +X beyond the beam face = deflection required to release

params.name: hook_height
params.description: height of the hook block (Z)

params.name: entry_angle
params.description: ramp angle on the top of the hook (lower = easier to push closed)

params.name: retention_angle
params.description: angle of the underside of the hook (90 = permanent, 45 = easy release)

params.name: root_fillet
params.description: fillet at the beam root to spread stress

material_notes.orientation: beam lying flat in the bed plane (beam length along X or Y, thickness along Z). Never print the beam standing up: bending then peels layers apart and the root cracks.
material_notes.notes: PETG and ABS/ASA flex reliably; PLA snaps below ~1.2 mm thickness or after a few dozen cycles. Strain at the root ~ 1.5*t*hook_depth/length^2 — keep under ~2% for PETG. Defaults give ~1.0%.

mechanisms.cantilever_latch.docstring:
The beam's back face is at x=0 (attach it there), hook faces +X.
Total height = length + hook_height.  As returned, the beam stands along
Z — that is the *assembled* pose for a latch embedded in a vertical wall,
and it must be rotated so the beam lies in the bed plane before printing
(see material_notes).  The usual layer-safe layout is to make the beam a
strip of the box wall: cut a U-slot in the wall, place the latch in it
with its length along the wall and its thickness = wall thickness, hook
pointing outward; the lid carries a skirt tab with a ``latch_window``.

Example:
    # beam runs along X inside the +Y wall (wall thickness = latch thickness), hook points +Y
    latch = Rot(0, 90, 90) * cantilever_latch(length=12, thickness=wall_t)
    body = body - wall_slot + Pos(x_root, y_wall, z_hook) * latch
    lid_tab = lid_tab - Pos(x_hook, y_wall, z_hook) * Rot(0, 0, 90) * latch_window(width=6, hook_depth=1.2)
mechanisms.cantilever_latch.example:
# beam runs along X inside the +Y wall (wall thickness = latch thickness), hook points +Y
latch = Rot(0, 90, 90) * cantilever_latch(length=12, thickness=wall_t)
body = body - wall_slot + Pos(x_root, y_wall, z_hook) * latch
lid_tab = lid_tab - Pos(x_hook, y_wall, z_hook) * Rot(0, 0, 90) * latch_window(width=6, hook_depth=1.2)

patterns.pi5_port_cutouts.docstring:
Rectangles to subtract from an enclosure wall so the Pi 5 connectors are reachable.

Sketch frame: x runs along the board edge in hole-pattern coordinates
(lib X for ``power``, lib Y for ``usb``/``sd``), y is height above the PCB
top surface.  Place it with ``Pos(x_of_pi_origin, z_of_pcb_top)`` on the
wall plane and extrude through the wall with ``both=True``.  ``gpio`` (v1.1.0) is
a window for a 40-way IDC socket and its ribbon on the +Y (header) edge.

Example:
    win = pi5_port_cutouts("power")
    body = body - extrude(Plane.XZ.offset(outer_w / 2) * Pos(pi_x, pcb_top_z) * win, amount=wall, both=True)
    gpio = pi5_port_cutouts("gpio")
    body = body - extrude(Plane.XZ.offset(-outer_w / 2) * Pos(pi_x, pcb_top_z) * gpio, amount=wall, both=True)
patterns.pi5_port_cutouts.example:
win = pi5_port_cutouts("power")

body = body - extrude(Plane.XZ.offset(-outer_w / 2) * Pos(pi_x, pcb_top_z) * gpio, amount=wall, both=True)

params.name: corner_r
params.description: outer vertical corner radius

params.name: bottom_chamfer
params.description: chamfer on the bed-contact edge (elephant foot)

params.name: inner_fillet
params.description: fillet where floor meets the inner walls (0 = none)

material_notes.orientation: floor on the bed, open top up

primitives.rounded_box.docstring:
Example:
body = rounded_box(110, 80, 35, wall=2.0)
body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * bosses
primitives.rounded_box.example:

body = body + Pos(0, 0, floor_t) * bosses

primitives.rubber_foot_recess.summary: Negative (subtract me) shallow recess to locate a stick-on rubber foot; top face at z=0, extends down.

params.name: d
params.description: rubber foot diameter

params.name: depth
params.description: recess depth

params.name: clearance
params.description: added to diameter

material_notes.orientation: any

primitives.rubber_foot_recess.docstring:
Example:
body = body - [loc * rubber_foot_recess(10) for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]
primitives.rubber_foot_recess.example: body = body - [loc * rubber_foot_recess(10) for loc in GridLocations(80, 50, 2, 2)]

primitives.socket_array.summary: Negative (subtract me): row or grid of blind cylindrical sockets with chamfered lead-ins; socket rims at z=0, bores extend down.

params.name: bore_d
params.description: nominal diameter of the object being held, before clearance

params.name: depth
params.description: socket depth from the rim (z=0) down to the bore floor

params.name: count
params.description: sockets along X

params.name: pitch
params.description: centre-to-centre along X

params.name: rows
params.description: socket rows along Y

params.name: row_pitch
params.description: centre-to-centre along Y; default = pitch

params.name: clearance
params.description: added to the DIAMETER (0.6 = 0.3 per side, drops in one-handed; 0.3 = snug)

params.name: lead_in
params.description: 45 degree chamfer at the rim so the object finds the hole; 0 = sharp rim

params.name: vent_d
params.description: coaxial hole through the bore floor for dust / pushing a stuck item out; 0 = blind

params.name: vent_len
params.description: how far the vent runs below the bore floor (make it reach the underside)

material_notes.orientation: bores vertical (axis along Z), rims up: the lead-in cone is a 45 deg overhang and each bore floor is an up-facing floor, so nothing needs support
material_notes.notes: UNVALIDATED: no test print yet. Clearance is added to the DIAMETER, not per side. Leave vent_d at 0 for anything that can leak — a vent under the pocket drips onto the desk.

primitives.socket_array.docstring:
Sockets on a ``count`` x ``rows`` grid centred on the origin, rims in the z=0 plane.

Subtract from a body whose top face is at ``top_z``::

    block = block - Pos(x, y, top_z) * socket_array(...)

The wall left between two sockets is ``pitch - bore_d - clearance``; keep it at 2 mm or more
(5 perimeters at a 0.4 nozzle) for anything that gets pushed sideways.

Example:
    holder = block - Pos(0, 0, block_h) * socket_array(11.0, depth=22, count=2, pitch=26)
primitives.socket_array.example: holder = block - Pos(0, 0, block_h) * socket_array(11.0, depth=22, count=2, pitch=26)

primitives.teardrop.summary: Teardrop hole profile (circle with a pointed top) so a horizontal-axis hole bridges without support; subtract from a vertical wall.

params.name: d
params.description: nominal hole diameter

params.name: angle
params.description: half-angle of the point (45 = printable without support)

params.name: print_oversize
params.description: FDM oversize

material_notes.orientation: hole axis horizontal, point up (+Y in the sketch)

primitives.teardrop.docstring:
Drawn in XY with the point in +Y; map onto the wall plane (e.g. Plane.XZ) so +Y becomes up.

Example:
    wall = wall - extrude(Plane.XZ * Pos(x, z) * teardrop(cable_d), amount=wall_t, both=True)
primitives.teardrop.example: wall = wall - extrude(Plane.XZ * Pos(x, z) * teardrop(cable_d), amount=wall_t, both=True)

primitives.vent_slots.summary: Grid of rounded ventilation slots filling a rectangular area, centred on the origin (subtract from a wall).

params.name: area_l
params.description: length of the vented area along the slots

params.name: area_w
params.description: width across the slots

params.name: slot_w
params.description: slot width (>= 1.5 for reliable bridging / cleaning)

params.name: pitch
params.description: centre-to-centre across slots (web = pitch - slot_w, keep >= 1.2)

params.name: slot_l
params.description: slot length; default fills area_l

params.name: rows
params.description: number of slot columns along the length; default 1

params.name: rotation
params.description: rotate the whole pattern in-plane

material_notes.orientation: on a vertical wall run slots vertically so they need no bridging

primitives.vent_slots.docstring:
Example:
side = side - extrude(Plane.XZ * vent_slots(40, 16), amount=wall, both=True)
primitives.vent_slots.example: side = side - extrude(Plane.XZ * vent_slots(40, 16), amount=wall, both=True)
